title: CALL "NAME" vs CALL WS-NAME — static link vs runtime resolution; different binding semantics
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PLUGIN-DISPATCH.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-PLUGIN  PIC X(8).
      *> CALL "FOO" resolves at link time: "FOO" must be a known
      *> program in the load module. CALL WS-PLUGIN resolves at run
      *> time -- WS-PLUGIN holds the name. The legacy uses this for
      *> plugin-like dispatch; modules can be swapped without
      *> relink. Java's natural target is reflection or a
      *> ServiceLoader; the spec must surface the dynamic-link nature.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE "PROCESS1" TO WS-PLUGIN.
           CALL WS-PLUGIN.
           MOVE "PROCESS2" TO WS-PLUGIN.
           CALL WS-PLUGIN.
notes: Dynamic CALL is the COBOL plugin pattern. Java's reflection or ServiceLoader is the natural rewrite; the spec must capture the dispatch table (which strings map to which behaviour) so the rewrite enumerates all bindings.
